ASTRAELFORGED

Predictive Reality Intelligence

An experimental intelligence initiative by TheVisionForged

Tagline: Understand Reality. Simulate Possibilities. Anticipate Tomorrow.

I would build AstraelForged around one central idea:

What if we could construct a computational model of the world, understand how its systems interact, simulate different possible futures, and identify what is likely to happen next?
summary:
EarthSignal is a Predictive Earth Intelligence platform developed by AstraelForge, a research and engineering team under TheVisionForged. Initially focused on Lucknow, India, it transforms NASA environmental data into interactive scientific analysis, validated temperature outlooks and experimental climate scenarios.

Using NASA POWER reanalysis data, historical weather-station comparisons and statistical methods, EarthSignal investigates environmental patterns, evaluates uncertainty and explores hypothetical changes through six interactive simulation tools. Its temperature forecasting module is displayed only after demonstrating improvement over a simple baseline in chronological hold-out testing.

EarthSignal aims to make complex Earth-system information accessible, transparent and useful for understanding environmental change and exploring possible futures.
details:
EarthSignal: A Predictive Earth Intelligence System

1. The challenge

Environmental datasets contain valuable information about our planet, but interpreting long-term patterns, comparing data sources and understanding uncertainty can be difficult.

EarthSignal addresses this challenge by turning environmental data into an interactive scientific intelligence platform, initially focused on Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh, India.

2. Our solution

EarthSignal brings together historical environmental analysis, statistical validation, tested temperature forecasting and interactive scenario experimentation in one platform.

Its key capabilities are:

Historical Earth Intelligence

  • Analysis of daily NASA POWER temperature and precipitation data.
  • More than four decades of historical coverage.
  • Exploration of two nearby POWER grid cells around Lucknow.
  • Monthly and annual environmental visualizations.
  • Seasonal trends, sensitivity analysis and statistical diagnostics.

Scientific Validation

  • Comparison of NASA POWER temperature estimates with NOAA GSOD observations from Lucknow airport.
  • Examination of differences between the two data records.
  • Explicit treatment of missing data, source limitations and uncertainty.
  • Investigation of how trends depend on the selected grid cell and analysis period.

Anticipate — Tested Temperature Outlook

EarthSignal includes a daily-average temperature outlook for up to 30 days.

The forecasting method was evaluated using chronological development and hold-out periods. It was required to outperform damped persistence, a simple forecasting baseline, before results could be displayed.

The eastern Lucknow grid cell passed all 30 forecast horizons. The western cell passed horizons 1–29; the 30-day result is withheld.

Rainfall forecasts are not presented because the tested methods did not demonstrate sufficient skill beyond the short term.

Simulation Studio

Six interactive tools allow users to explore hypothetical environmental changes:

  1. Climate Scenario Builder.
  2. Heat Stress Explorer.
  3. Rainfall Stress Simulator.
  4. Compound Climate Experiment.
  5. Historical Analog Finder.
  6. Uncertainty and Sensitivity Lab.

The tools use historical NASA POWER data and explicitly documented transformations. Their results are labelled hypothetical or derived statistics, not observations or calibrated predictions.

3. Data and methodology

The principal environmental dataset is NASA POWER daily point data, using MERRA-2 and the subsequent GEOS-IT near-real-time extension.

Variables include:

  • T2M: average air temperature at two metres, °C.
  • PRECTOTCORR: bias-corrected total precipitation, mm/day.

The project also uses NOAA Global Summary of the Day data for a carefully qualified airport-station temperature comparison.

Scientific methods include:

  • Mann–Kendall trend testing with autocorrelation correction.
  • Sen's slope and confidence intervals.
  • Seasonal analysis and multiple-testing correction.
  • Start-year and end-year sensitivity analysis.
  • Chronological forecasting evaluation.
  • Historical resampling and scenario transformations.

4. Main findings

The analysis does not establish a robust monotonic temperature trend for Lucknow over 1981–2025.

The comparison between NASA POWER and the Lucknow airport temperature record identifies a divergence during 2006–2023. The analysis does not establish which record is responsible for the divergence.

Precipitation trends vary between grid cells and analysis periods. The project therefore avoids claiming that Lucknow is becoming wetter or drier.

The tested temperature outlook demonstrates modest improvements over a simple baseline, while clearly reporting its limitations and the fact that it is not an official weather forecast.

5. Innovation

EarthSignal connects historical environmental analysis, independent data comparison, forecasting evaluation and interactive scenario experimentation.

Rather than displaying model outputs without qualification, it makes methodology, uncertainty, provenance and limitations visible to users.

Its Simulation Studio allows users to investigate alternative assumptions using reproducible calculations on real historical datasets.

6. Potential impact

EarthSignal demonstrates a reusable approach for making Earth-system data more accessible and understandable.

Its architecture can be extended to additional environmental datasets and geographic regions, supporting future research into climate variability, environmental monitoring and evidence-based decision support.

7. Limitations and future work

Current limitations include:

  • The initial geographic focus is Lucknow and its available grid cells.
  • Temperature forecasts are available; validated rainfall forecasts are not.
  • Scenario experiments are hypothetical transformations, not causal Earth-system simulations.
  • The precipitation record requires additional independent validation.
  • Further datasets are needed for flood, air-quality, soil-moisture, crop and urban-impact modelling.

EarthSignal's longer-term vision is to develop an integrated Predictive Earth Intelligence platform that connects observation, scientific analysis, modelling, simulation and learning from new evidence.

NASA POWER — Prediction Of Worldwide Energy Resources

Resource: https://power.larc.nasa.gov/

Product: Daily Point API
API version recorded in the project: v2.10.3

Variables:

  • T2M — average air temperature at 2 metres (°C).
  • PRECTOTCORR — bias-corrected total precipitation (mm/day).

Geographic focus: Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh, India, using two nearby POWER grid cells.

Historical coverage: 1 January 1981 – 13 November 2026 (latest acquired dataset; valid values through 11 November 2026).

Data sources reported by the API: MERRA-2 and GEOS-IT, with the documented transition between sources.

Application: Historical trend analysis, environmental visualization, statistical validation, temperature forecasting evaluation and hypothetical scenario experimentation.

NASA POWER values are reanalysis-derived estimates, not direct ground-station measurements.

NOAA Global Summary of the Day (GSOD)
https://www.ncei.noaa.gov/data/global-summary-of-the-day/

Used for a qualified temperature comparison with Lucknow airport station 42369099999.

Technology and development:

  • Python
  • FastAPI
  • React
  • TypeScript
  • Vite
  • Pandas
  • NumPy
  • SciPy
  • Plotly
